THE FULL IT/OT PICTURE

From business systems to the machines on your floor.

IT supports the business: its applications, servers, users, and office network. OT supports production: the systems that monitor and control equipment. This diagram shows how those layers connect, with controlled access between business and industrial networks.

The Purdue Model: understanding the IT/OT boundary

The Purdue Model groups systems by their role, from enterprise applications at Level 5 to the physical process at Level 0. An industrial DMZ at Level 3.5 provides a controlled boundary between business and plant networks.

Download 11 × 17 PDF ↗ Download editable Visio ↗

Free downloads hosted on GitHub. For a more detailed infrastructure example, view the CPwE reference architecture from Cisco, Panduit, and Rockwell Automation’s February 2023 guide.

BUSINESS IT · LEVELS 4–5

Run the business

Business applications, email, identity services, servers, and connections to the internet and cloud.

IT/OT BOUNDARY · LEVEL 3.5

Control the connections

An industrial demilitarized zone (IDMZ) separates business and plant networks and controls the services and traffic passing between them.

SITE OPERATIONS · LEVEL 3

Connect the plant

Plant applications, servers, core switches, and distribution links connect production areas and make operational information available.

MACHINES & PROCESSES · LEVELS 0–2

Monitor and control equipment

Controllers, operator screens, sensors, drives, and industrial switches connect at the machine and production-line level.

Where we help

We work on the connections and records that tie these systems together. Start with the part of your operation that needs attention:

  • Office networks and Wi-Fi — investigate connection problems and plan equipment changes on the business side.
  • Plant network infrastructure — connect equipment and production areas, configure switches and traffic separation, and review copper, fiber, cabinets, and redundant paths.
  • Drawings and handover records — map connections across the site, identify cables and ports, and document the work for IT and maintenance teams.

For connections across the IT/OT boundary, we coordinate the network requirements and responsibilities with your IT team, controls staff, and equipment vendors.

Discuss the systems you need connected →

Working around production

Plan the change before touching the network.

A plant network connects equipment that people depend on to do their work. Before agreeing to changes, we discuss the production schedule, affected systems, and the people who need to be involved.

Check the site conditions

Review equipment locations, cable distances, and exposure to heat, dust, moisture, vibration, or electrical noise. Plan the connections and access your team will need to maintain them.

Coordinate with your team

Identify the maintenance, IT, and equipment-vendor contacts involved. Agree on access requirements and suitable work windows before scheduling.

Agree on testing and recovery

Define how a proposed change will be checked and how the previous setup can be restored if the checks fail.

Leave a clear record

Update the agreed drawings, cable labels, and connection records. Record the checks performed and anything still unresolved for your IT and maintenance teams.

From first conversation to completed work.

You should know what you are buying, what happens next, and who is responsible at each stage.

  1. 01

    Describe the need

    Tell us what is happening, the systems involved, your location, and your preferred timing. We confirm whether the project is a fit and what information is needed.

  2. 02

    Agree on the scope

    Define the assessment or implementation work, deliverables, cost, and schedule before the project starts.

  3. 03

    Carry out the work

    Work follows the agreed scope. Proposed additions or changes are discussed with you, including their effect on cost and timing.

  4. 04

    Review and hand over

    Review the results, receive the agreed records, and identify any remaining issues or recommended actions.

An assessment and a repair are different purchases.

You can start with an investigation or discuss implementation from the outset. We make clear which work is included in the quote and which decisions need your approval.
